blocks.text: Configuration drift is the gradual divergence of servers that should be identical, caused by manual, unrecorded changes; a snowflake server is one whose exact state can no longer be reproduced.

items: Hotfixes applied by SSH during incidents and never written down.
Package upgrades run on some hosts but not others.
Different install dates → different package versions.

rows: State lives outside (DBs, volumes, object storage)

items: A failed snowflake can't be rebuilt reliably, so outages last longer.
Bugs appear on one node only and are impossible to reproduce.
Scaling out means copying an unknown configuration.
Audits and security patching become guesswork.

blocks.text: Build an immutable image, deploy it, and replace it rather than patch it. `docker exec` fixes are drift in miniature: they vanish on recreate, which is the point.

Q: "What's the difference between pets and cattle, and why does it matter?" A: "Pets are mutable servers maintained by hand, so they drift into unreproducible snowflakes. Cattle are immutable, built from a definition, and replaced rather than repaired. Containers make the cattle model cheap: rebuild the image, redeploy, and roll back by redeploying the previous tag."

items: Immutable artifacts are replaced, not patched.
Keep state outside the replaceable unit.
